title: Database and Persistence Technical Reference
readerIntent: Audit persistence ownership, provider capabilities, configuration, and verification.
owner: Nodics database contracts and selected provider
summary: Technical changes must preserve schema authority, generated model behavior, tenant resolution, access policy, lifecycle, and provider abstraction.

sections.heading: Authority and provider boundary
items: Generated item models and model-handler services provide provider-neutral record interaction; nDatabase selects adapters; business modules own schemas and invariants.
Adapters own connections, pools, transactions, indexes, query mapping, vendor errors, readiness, reconnect, and shutdown without exporting vendor types to callers.
AI, frontend, imports, jobs, and other modules never open direct database connections around this boundary.

sections.heading: Resolution and configuration
items: Layered properties resolve provider and connection aliases by environment, module, tenant, and supported scope with explicit defaults and provenance.
Endpoints, TLS, pool, timeout, retry, database names, and secret references are configuration; credentials and machine-local paths never enter committed defaults.
An adapter declares truthful capabilities so callers fail clearly when transactions, indexes, query operators, or data types are unsupported.

sections.heading: Data lifecycle
items: Schema loading creates or validates models and indexes through existing framework services; ordinary create, read, update, delete, and search preserve tenant and authorization context.
Imports, migrations, and runtime changes use the same schema and service authorities, batching, idempotency, audit, and recovery rather than collection scripts.
Successful authoritative changes coordinate cache invalidation, search indexing, events, workflows, and publishing according to owned lifecycle contracts.

sections.heading: Operations and recovery
items: Monitor connection, pool saturation, query latency, errors, conflicts, transaction abort, index build, migration, storage, replication, and backup with safe labels.
Test authentication failure, network partition, reconnect, primary change, timeout, pool exhaustion, duplicate key, transaction uncertainty, shutdown, backup/restore, and upgrade.
Document supported versions, capacity, consistency, backup objectives, encryption, credential rotation, migration, failover, restore verification, and provider removal.

sections.heading: Contract checklist
items: Provider identity and truthful capability declaration.
Layered connection aliases, handlers, pool, timeout, retry, TLS, and secret references.
Tenant/module database resolution and model isolation.
Schema, index, CRUD, query, middleware, relationship, and transaction mappings.
Normalized errors, diagnostics, readiness, reconnect, and shutdown.
Import, export, cache, search, event, audit, and runtime-governance interactions.

sections.heading: Verification matrix
items: Positive CRUD/query and transactions where supported.
Negative configuration, authentication, authorization, validation, conflict, and provider failures.
Boundary sizes, pagination, batching, timeouts, pool limits, and tenant counts.
Provider-neutral contract and live integration.
Backup, restore, failover, migration, performance, security, and regression.
Verify owning schema and service behavior across every production-qualified provider, not only connectivity.
